c.tagline: Korea's ancient Silla capital — royal tombs, stone temples and a thousand years of history in the open air.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are standard and honest; hailing through the Kakao T app is easiest since few drivers speak English. Base fares are low but the KTX station and Bulguksa are far enough out to add up.

emergency.note: 112 reaches police and 119 covers fire and ambulance; both have English-language assistance.

hood_desc: The walkable heart of old Gyeongju around Daereungwon (Tumuli Park), Cheomseongdae observatory, and the Gyeongju National Museum; grassy royal burial mounds sit between the streets and everything lights up at dusk. Best for first-timers who want the Silla sights on foot.

A trendy cafe-and-boutique street beside the tomb park lined with modern coffee houses, dessert shops, hanok-style eateries and local art; the city's liveliest evening strip and a favorite for younger travelers.

A landscaped lakeside resort district a few kilometers east with international hotels, a golf course, cherry-blossom paths and cruise boats; calm, green and family-friendly, though a short drive from the historic core.

The forested temple area on the slopes of Tohamsan, home to UNESCO-listed Bulguksa Temple and Seokguram Grotto; staying here means quiet mountain surroundings and early temple access before the tour buses arrive.
The downtown grid around Seongdong Market and the bus terminal, packed with traditional-market stalls, cheap eats and everyday shops; a convenient, budget-friendly and authentically local base.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though most Koreans prefer bottled or filtered.

transit.hours: City and intercity buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:30 PM; there is no metro or tram, so taxis and ride apps cover late nights.
transit.note: Gyeongju has no subway; travel is by local city bus, sightseeing bus routes linking the main sites, and taxis. The KTX high-speed train stops at Singyeongju Station outside town.
transit.pay: Tap a T-money or Cashbee transit card (sold at convenience stores) on boarding, or pay cash to the driver (around W1,500 per ride). The same card works nationwide.

bus: Intercity/express buses to Busan, Seoul, Daegu and beyond
train: KTX high-speed rail via Singyeongju Station (Seoul in ~2h)
Mugunghwa/ITX regional trains via Gyeongju Station

airport.name: Ulsan Airport (USN) — nearest; Gimhae Int'l (PUS) and Daegu (TAE) also serve the city

transit.m: KTX from Seoul to Singyeongju Station (~2h), then 15-min taxi (~W15,000) to the historic center
Frequent intercity bus from Busan (~1h) to Gyeongju Bus Terminal
Limousine bus or taxi from Ulsan Airport (~40 min)

tip.r: Not expected anywhere; service is included and rounding up is unnecessary.
